_README: Corrections to model_type for dog and cat studies whose extracted value was
'mixed-or-not-stated' (amendment A10, limitation L90). The field decides whether a result
appears in the companion or the laboratory column, and an unfilled value was defaulting all of
them to laboratory. Each study below was resolved by reading its own full text; the quoted
phrase is the evidence. 'spontaneous-companion' = client-owned animals with naturally occurring
disease; 'induced' / 'healthy' = purpose-bred or laboratory animals, or a regulatory-database
Applied at build time, per study. The stored records keep what the extractor recorded.

19675678.why: 'Naturally occurring cancers in canines and humans share many [features]' — comparative study of spontaneous canine and human mammary tumours.

25075523.why: 'blood was collected for diagnostic purposes from healthy dogs (n = 26) or mammary tumor-bearing [dogs]' — clinical canine patients, and the paper calls for 'clinical investigations using spontaneous tumor models'.

25671556.why: 'Spontaneous canine models exist for several inherited retinal dystrophies' — but these are maintained research colonies of affected dogs used for gene-therapy dosing, not client-owned patients. Laboratory column, as the dog side of the RPE65 comparison.

26753942.why: Analysis of regulatory preclinical toxicity testing across species: 'Preclinical trials or animal tests on new drugs are required by regulatory agencies worldwide'. Laboratory animals by definition.

29730448.why: PharmaPendium analysis of 'preclinical safety-related observations' in regulatory submissions over 70 years. Laboratory toxicology studies.

30188888.why: 'Naturally-occurring canine cancers'; 'Spontaneous canine malignant melanomas'; explicitly about 'improving lives of pet dogs'.

30364994.why: Compounds 'tested in 1-month toxicity studies' under the 'current nonclinical testing paradigm'. Regulatory laboratory studies.

30823899.why: Argues about 'the current regulatory paradigm of animal testing', drawing on 'the largest database of animal and human toxicity studies yet compiled'. Laboratory toxicology.

30837603.why: 'Forty-one tumor-bearing, 37 inflammatory, and 31 healthy dogs were recruited at the RVC' — clinical patients at veterinary hospitals, with 'dogs with spontaneous tumors' as the stated subject.

30925701.why: 'the first study that has evaluated genomic imbalances in a cohort of dogs with spontaneous PC'.

33282730.why: 'Canine mammary tumors are a naturally occurring heterogeneous group of cancers'; dogs described as 'powerful spontaneous models of cancer'.

33304937.why: Meta-analysis of studies in 'Naturally occurring canine invasive urothelial carcinoma' and 'naturally occurring canine cancer', including a case-control study 'In pet dogs'.

37391533.why: 'stromal reprogramming in benign and malignant naturally occurring [canine mammary tumours]'; 'canine spontaneous' tumours throughout.

38166662.why: 'this canine disease as a naturally occurring model for human PTCL'; 'the dog as a naturally occurring preclinical model of this disease'.

40443661.why: 'samples were obtained with owner consent from residual tissues of canine patients'; 'Companion dogs with spontaneous cancer have been validated as models of human disease'.

41208961.why: 'Dogs develop spontaneous cancers with striking similarities to human [cancers]'; soft tissue sarcoma in dogs compared with healthy tissue.

41279656.why: 'sampling was performed with informed owner consent where applicable'; canine cruciate ligament rupture is naturally occurring, compared against human ACL and TKA patients.

41395361.why: 'dogs spontaneously develop mucosal melanomas that resemble the clinical, histological [features of human melanoma]'; a clinical canine eyelid melanoma case.

42218196.why: 'veterinarians — with informed consent from their owners — collected opportunistic samples of spontaneously occurring mammary [tumours]' at a university small animal clinic.

W4241628985.why: Canine inflammatory bowel disease as 'the spontaneous model for studying mechanisms'; clinical cases contrasted with healthy Beagles and Greyhounds.
